protocols.title: Loose-lead walking — reward check-ins (draft, force-free)
protocols.intendedOutcome: Dog chooses proximity and soft lead through reinforcement of check-ins and slack-lead moments, without relying on forward motion as the primary consequence for tight lead.
prerequisites: Comfort with harness and light lead indoors
protocols.environment: Quiet indoor or low-distraction outdoor space.
protocols.baselineAssessment: Dog accepts harness and short indoor lead walking.

steps.instruction: Walk indoors or in a quiet area; mark and reward any moment the lead is soft while your dog is near you.
steps.rewardTiming: Reward at your side when the lead is slack.
steps.progressCriteria: Several soft-lead moments per minute in a quiet space.
steps.easierIfStruggling: Higher-value rewards; shorter distance; stationary rewards for proximity.
failureModes: Practising in high distraction before basics are solid

steps.instruction: When your dog checks in or the lead loosens, reward generously; if the lead tightens, pause politely and wait for slack without jerking.
steps.rewardTiming: Reward check-ins and slack before moving on.
steps.progressCriteria: Dog offers more frequent check-ins and soft lead in low distraction.
steps.easierIfStruggling: Stop sooner; end session after a few successes.
failureModes: Pulling handler forward to create slack

safetyPrecautions: Do not use equipment designed to cause pain or fear.
Seek local reward-based help if walks feel unsafe.
protocols.reviewReason: Draft alternative for Good Dog P1-1 method review; not for blind sync over ex-lead-loose.
